_comment: Integration-owned (contract SHARED files list + coordinator's
integration-cost-decisions.md decision 2, 2026-09-06). This file is NOT one
of the seven <lane>.json catalog fragments registry.load_catalog() iterates
-- manifests/catalog/index.json's 'ids' mapping names exactly core, measurement,
protocol, registry, adapter, redteam, integration, so a sibling file with a
different name is invisible to load_catalog and cannot collide with it.
Why this lives here instead of as a 'heavy_external' key directly on the
affected CatalogEntry objects (the coordinator's literal wording):
framework/registry.py (registry lane, not integration-owned; contract section
6 ownership map) parses each catalog-entry JSON object against a FIXED field
tuple (_CATALOG_ENTRY_FIELDS) and raises CatalogUnresolvable on any key
outside it. Adding 'heavy_external' straight onto a fragment entry would break
load_catalog for every ID in that fragment -- not just gate the slow ones --
the moment any fragment carried the key. Integration's hard-rule scope for
this delivery is 'contract section 6 shared files, evals/redteam/run.sh, any
manifests/catalog/<lane>.json to add the optional heavy_external key, and any
test module' -- it does NOT include framework/registry.py, so extending
CatalogEntry's schema is out of scope here. This file delivers decision 2's
functional intent (a fast, documented exclusion set consulted by --gate)
without touching a non-owned file or weakening any lane's parsing.
See integration-report.md for the full account and the per-test evidence
(promptfoo validate / promptfoo eval / docker netproof calls) that justifies
each ID below.

heavy_external.T42: PinnedVersionAndConfigValidity.test_wrapper_reports_pinned_version_and_validates_every_config runs `promptfoo validate` against every committed redteam config (~30 files) via bin/promptfoo.sh -- a real subprocess per config.
heavy_external.T43: ProviderApiConformance.test_promptfoo_actually_invokes_the_custom_provider runs a real `promptfoo eval` over configs/offline-stub.yaml through the pinned entrypoint.
heavy_external.T45: SafeVulnerableControls.setUpClass runs THREE real `promptfoo eval` passes (control-safe, control-vulnerable, control-refusenik x 32 rows each) before any test method in the class executes.
heavy_external.T48: OfflineDefaultDoesNotNetwork.test_docker_netproof_verifies_isolation spins up a real `docker run --network=none` container cycle (bin/netproof.sh).

not_flagged_and_why.T44: FrozenCorpusIntegrity.test_freeze_check_passes_on_the_committed_corpus is bin/freeze.py --check -- pure sha256 hashing over committed files, no promptfoo/docker. Kept in --gate per the integration brief.
not_flagged_and_why.T46: TwoByTwoCompleteness's CATALOG-MAPPED method (test_two_by_two_design_has_four_balanced_cells_with_shared_corpus_and_grader) reads committed configs/generated/_index.json and calls generate.check_dominance() -- no subprocess call. (Its sibling test_generated_configs_are_not_drifted DOES shell out to generate.py --check and would be heavy, but that sibling is not T46's catalog resolution target per contract section 7.3/7.4 -- see manifests/catalog/redteam.json's own _comment.) Already excluded from --gate anyway: approval_gate=paid-required.
not_flagged_and_why.T47: ProtectedEffectDominanceAndNativeGate's catalog-mapped test reads only committed JSON row fixtures under fixtures/ledgers/** and calls bin/verdict.py in-process -- no subprocess call.
not_flagged_and_why.T23: McpInspectReadOnly already carries requires_real_marketplace: true in manifests/catalog/protocol.json (it spawns the real plugins/agent-compiler MCP server) and is therefore already excluded from --gate by the existing rrm exclusion; heavy_external is not needed for it. It is fast (a single stdio round trip) when it does run under --offline/--catalog.

_resolved_2026-09-06: requires_real_marketplace_undeclared (T14,T15,T16,T17) was folded into manifests/catalog/registry.json by the coordinator; the empirical evidence lives in integration-report.md section 5.
